title: Norwegian citizens distinguish usable public services from weak influence, administrative trust, and confidence in automated decisions
source_unit: Norwegian Agency for Public and Financial Management (DFØ), Innbyggerundersøkelsen 2026 (Citizen Survey 2026)
geography: Norway; national citizen survey with municipal and national public-service modules, using weighted results and repeated 2010-2025 trend tables

observations.period: 2021-2025; trust in national government and public administration

denominator.unit: Norwegian Citizen Survey 2025 respondents for government trust item; administration item N=16021

government_high_trust.unit: percent reporting high trust in government in 2025, compared with 64% in 2021

government_low_trust.unit: percent reporting low trust in government in 2025, compared with 22% in 2021

administration_high_trust.unit: percent reporting high trust in public administration in 2025, compared with 62% in 2021

administration_low_trust.unit: percent reporting low trust in public administration in 2025, compared with 19% in 2021

observations.method: Official Norwegian Citizen Survey weighted repeated cross-section results, with comparable 2021 and 2025 trust measures.
observations.uncertainty: The survey documents changes in reported trust but does not identify causal drivers, establish that all respondents experienced the same institutions, or separate national political events from administrative encounters.
observations.subgroup: Norwegian adult respondents in the 2021 and 2025 survey waves; the published table reports aggregate results for these items.
observations.counterinterpretation: Trust can move with salient national events or survey context even when day-to-day public services remain stable; the decline does not by itself prove worsening service performance.

observations.period: 2025; public service quality alongside local political voice

denominator.unit: Norwegian Citizen Survey respondents for municipal-service quality and local-politician listening items

municipal_service_satisfaction.unit: percent satisfied with the quality of municipal services

local_politician_listening.unit: percent satisfied with how municipal politicians listen to residents' views

local_politician_dissatisfaction.unit: percent dissatisfied with how municipal politicians listen to residents' views

local_influence.unit: percent saying the Norwegian political system gives people like them much influence, versus 44% saying little influence

observations.method: Official Norwegian Citizen Survey weighted cross-sectional results combining municipal service assessment, local representation, and political-influence questions.
observations.uncertainty: These are separate descriptive questions and do not establish that service quality causes or offsets political dissatisfaction; the influence item is national while the listening item is municipal.
observations.subgroup: Norwegian residents assessing municipal services and local political representation.
observations.counterinterpretation: Citizens may judge service delivery and political responsiveness by different standards; a reasonably usable service can coexist with disagreement over representation or policy outcomes.

denominator.unit: Norwegian Citizen Survey respondents in the 2025 public-institution expectation module; item Ns approximately 4685-4690

complaint_improvement.unit: percent saying it is likely that a public service improves when many people complain, down from 32% in 2023

reform_explanation.unit: percent saying it is likely that authorities explain how a reform affects them, versus 41% saying unlikely

local_decision_influence.unit: percent saying residents are likely to influence a decision affecting their local area, versus 52% saying unlikely

service_adaptation.unit: percent saying public services are likely to adapt quickly to changed social needs, versus 59% saying unlikely

observations.method: Official Norwegian Citizen Survey weighted cross-sectional expectations module, with a limited 2023 comparison for complaint responsiveness.
observations.uncertainty: Perceived institutional responsiveness is not an observed count of reforms, complaint outcomes, or participation decisions; the questions measure expectations and the 2023-2025 comparison is not a causal panel.
observations.subgroup: Norwegian residents evaluating public responsiveness, reform communication, local influence, and adaptation to changing needs.
observations.counterinterpretation: Low expectations may reflect high standards or awareness of slow democratic processes rather than uniformly poor institutional performance; some changes may be invisible to respondents.

observations.period: 2025; confidence in artificial intelligence used by public bodies

denominator.unit: Norwegian Citizen Survey respondents for the public-sector AI tailored-service item; fairness item N=4664

tailored_services_confidence.unit: percent confident public AI will deliver services better tailored to individual needs, versus 44% unconfident

fair_treatment_confidence.unit: percent confident AI systems will treat different groups fairly, versus 51% unconfident

uncertainty.value: 14-16% selected neither confident nor unconfident and 7-9% did not know on these items

observations.method: Official Norwegian Citizen Survey weighted cross-sectional questions on anticipated public-sector AI performance and fairness.
observations.uncertainty: These are expectations about future or unfamiliar public-sector AI use, not measured algorithmic performance, realized discrimination, or evidence that confidence changes after deployment.
observations.subgroup: Norwegian residents evaluating public-sector AI personalization and equal treatment.
observations.counterinterpretation: Skepticism may reflect prudent demand for safeguards rather than opposition to useful automation; higher knowledge or direct exposure could change views.

related_sources.claim: Official DFØ workbook containing the 2010-2025 weighted tables and 2025 public-service, representation, and AI questions.
OECD Trust Survey provides a cross-country comparator for the Norway citizen-survey results.

boundary: This record adds a Norwegian comparative public-service, political-voice, and public-sector-AI trust route. It uses official weighted survey tables and repeated cross-sectional comparisons, not respondent-level longitudinal data, observed service outcomes, causal explanations, or evidence that AI has been deployed and evaluated in these services.

reproduction_audit.retrieval_hash_scope: The official DFØ 2026 Citizen Survey page and downloadable workbook were reviewed for trust trends, municipal service quality, local listening and influence, responsiveness expectations, reform explanation, service adaptation, and public-sector AI confidence.
